itinerary.title: Departure from Delhi
itinerary.body:
Overnight Journey to Manali
Your journey begins in the evening as the group departs from Delhi in an AC Volvo/Tempo Traveller. The overnight drive takes you through the changing landscapes of North India toward the mountains of Himachal Pradesh.
Highlights
Departure around 7:00–8:00 PM
Comfortable overnight road journey
Pit stop for dinner at a roadside restaurant (self-paid)
Pickup available from Delhi/Chandigarh
The excitement builds as you leave the city lights behind and head toward the Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Manali & Local Exploration
itinerary.body:
Stay: Hotel in Manali
After arriving in Manali, check into your hotel and relax for a while after the overnight journey. Surrounded by pine forests and snow-covered peaks, Manali offers the perfect mountain escape.
Places Covered
Hadimba Devi Temple
Visit the famous Hadimba Temple, one of Manali’s most iconic attractions, located amidst tall deodar forests. The peaceful atmosphere and unique wooden architecture make it a must-visit.
Van Vihar
Take a leisurely walk through Van Vihar, a beautiful forest area known for its greenery and calm environment.
Old Manali Café Hopping
Explore the charming lanes of Old Manali filled with vibrant cafés, live music spots, bakeries, and mountain-style eateries. Enjoy local food, coffee, and the relaxed backpacker vibe.
Mall Road
Spend the evening exploring Mall Road, where you can:
Shop for souvenirs and woollens
Try Himachali street food
Enjoy the lively local atmosphere
Meals Included
Dinner
Overnight Stay
Hotel in Manali

itinerary.title: Manali to Jispa via Atal Tunnel & Baralacha La
itinerary.body:
Stay: Swiss Camps in Jispa
Wake up to a beautiful mountain morning and enjoy breakfast before beginning one of the most scenic drives of the trip.
Major Attractions
Atal Tunnel
Drive through the iconic Atal Tunnel, one of the world’s longest highway tunnels at high altitude. As you cross into the Lahaul Valley, witness a dramatic shift in landscapes—from green valleys to barren Himalayan terrain.
Lahaul Valley
Enjoy panoramic views of rugged mountains, winding roads, and river valleys that make this route incredibly photogenic.
Baralacha La Pass
Continue toward Baralacha La, one of the highest motorable mountain passes in India situated on the Manali–Leh Highway at over 16,000 ft. Snow-covered peaks and vast mountain landscapes make this stretch unforgettable.
Suraj Tal
Visit the stunning Suraj Tal Lake, a crystal-clear high-altitude lake surrounded by dramatic Himalayan scenery. The lake is known for its surreal beauty and peaceful environment.
Arrival in Jispa
Reach Jispa by evening and check into Swiss camps near the riverside. Relax amidst the cold mountain breeze and scenic surroundings.
Evening Experience
Bonfire and music (weather permitting)
Stargazing opportunity
Peaceful Himalayan camping experience
Meals Included
Breakfast
Dinner
Overnight Stay
Swiss Camps in Jispa

itinerary.title: Jispa to Manali via Sissu | Departure for Delhi
itinerary.body:
Overnight Journey
Wake up early and enjoy breakfast surrounded by Himalayan views before checking out from the camps.
Sissu Village Exploration
On the way back toward Manali, stop at the beautiful village of Sissu, known for:
Snow-clad mountain views
Waterfalls and riverside scenery
Adventure activities (at personal expense)
Scenic photography spots
Spend some time exploring this peaceful Himalayan hamlet before continuing the drive back to Manali.
Evening Departure
In the evening, board your overnight vehicle back to Delhi with unforgettable memories of the Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Reach Delhi
itinerary.body: Arrive back in Delhi by morning, marking the end of your memorable Manali–Jispa adventure.

Jibhi Waterfall
Nestled amidst dense pine forests, Jibhi Waterfall is one of the most peaceful attractions in the valley. The short walk

Mini Thailand
A unique natural formation where giant rocks create a beautiful river passage, often known as the "Mini Thailand of

significance among locals.

Pradesh, offering breathtaking views of the Great Himalayan Range.

A beautiful forest trek passing through dense oak and deodar forests, offering stunning Himalayan landscapes
throughout the route.

Bonfire & Group Activities.

Serolsar Lake

untouched natural beauty, making it one of the most beautiful lakes in Himachal Pradesh.
Budhi Nagin Temple
Located beside Serolsar Lake, this sacred temple holds great religious importance among local communities and adds
a spiritual charm to the trek.
• Return to Jalori Pass.

Known for its crystal-clear river, charming villages, trout-filled streams, and scenic landscapes, Tirthan Valley is one of
Himachal Pradesh's most peaceful destinations.

Riverside Experience
Relax beside the flowing Tirthan River, enjoy photography, explore local cafes, and soak in the beauty of the valley.

packages.summaryFromDelhi:
Overview
Embark on a breathtaking journey through the pristine landscapes of Himachal Pradesh with Tripwaley’s specially
curated Bir Billing Barot Tour Package. This unforgettable trip takes you through the charming Tibetan settlements of
Bir, the thrilling heights of Billing, and the serene beauty of Barot Valley.
Whether you seek adventure, spirituality, relaxation, or peaceful mountain vibes, this journey offers the perfect
blend of thrilling experiences and natural beauty. From colorful monasteries and Tibetan culture to pine forests,
waterfalls, rivers, and scenic valleys — every moment of this trip is designed to create unforgettable memories.

About Bir
Bir is a picturesque town nestled in the beautiful Kangra Valley of Himachal Pradesh. It is globally famous as the
second-highest paragliding destination in the world and is known for its peaceful Tibetan culture, monasteries, cafés,
and mountain views.
Bir is home to several monasteries and meditation centers that attract spiritual seekers and travelers from all over
the world. The famous Palpung Sherabling Monastery is one of the largest monasteries in Himachal Pradesh and
offers mesmerizing Tibetan architecture and peaceful surroundings. Travelers can also explore Chokling Monastery
and Nyingma Monastery, both known for their colorful Buddhist artwork and spiritual atmosphere.
The famous Deer Park Institute gives travelers an opportunity to learn about Buddhist philosophy and Tibetan
traditions. Nature lovers can enjoy peaceful walks to Bangoru Waterfall surrounded by lush greenery and mountain
scenery.

About Barot Valley
Barot Valley is a hidden paradise known for its untouched natural beauty, pine forests, rivers, and peaceful mountain
atmosphere. The valley is famous for trout fishing in the crystal-clear waters of the Uhl River and for scenic nature
walks surrounded by cedar and pine forests.
Travelers can also explore Nargu Wildlife Sanctuary, home to Himalayan Monals, Black Bears, Ghorals, and rich
Himalayan wildlife.

Enjoy bonfire & music night amidst the mountains

Dehradun is the capital city of Uttarakhand and is famous for its peaceful atmosphere, waterfalls, caves, temples,

weekend travelers.

• Pleasant weather throughout the year

• Local markets & cafes
• Gateway to hill stations and Char Dham routes

Mussoorie is popularly known as the “Queen of Hills.” It is famous for its breathtaking mountain views, cold
weather, waterfalls, cafes, Mall Road, and peaceful hill station vibes.
Travelers love Mussoorie because of:
• Snow-covered Himalayan views
• Beautiful waterfalls like Kempty Falls

Ancient Shiva temple situated inside a cave where natural water continuously falls on the Shivling.

Famous local market for shopping, food, cafes, and evening walks.

Most famous waterfall in Mussoorie where travelers can enjoy water fun and beautiful nature.

Best place for shopping, cafés, local food, and enjoying Mussoorie’s evening vibe.

A popular viewpoint offering stunning Himalayan and Doon Valley views.

Peaceful road famous for nature walks and sunset views.

Beautiful garden with flowers, boating area, cafes, and family attractions.
• Evening free for leisure and café hopping.
• Dinner & overnight stay in Mussoorie.

• Check-out from hotel.

Highest point in Mussoorie famous for breathtaking Himalayan views.

Popular viewpoint and trekking location surrounded by greenery and mountains.

packages.name: Kashmir — Shikara Days, Gulmarg Nights
packages.summaryFromDelhi:
KASHMIR HONEYMOON — SRINAGAR, GULMARG & PAHALGAM
5 Nights / 6 Days · Private trip for two

The one everybody pictures when they say honeymoon, done without the crowds. Two nights on a cedar-panelled houseboat on Dal Lake, a morning shikara ride while the lake is still glass, the Gulmarg gondola above the treeline, and two unhurried days in the Betaab valley at Pahalgam.

No group, no fixed roll call. A private cab and driver stay with you for the whole trip, so the day starts when you're ready for it to start.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
The houseboat is booked whole, not by the room. The Pahalgam property is chosen for the valley-facing balcony, not the star rating. And your planner has personally stayed in both.
packages.socialProof: Booked it three days after the wedding. The shikara at 6 AM with nobody else on the lake is the photo we printed.
packages.scarcityNote: Houseboats book out 6–8 weeks ahead for the tulip season.
inclusions: 5 nights stay — 2 on a private Dal Lake houseboat, 3 in valley-facing hotels
Daily breakfast and dinner for two
Private cab with driver for the entire trip
Airport pickup and drop at Srinagar
One-hour private shikara ride on Dal Lake
Flower-decorated room on the night you arrive
Gulmarg gondola phase-1 tickets for two
All tolls, parking and driver charges
exclusions: Pony rides and local guides at Betaab / Aru valley

itinerary.title: Land in Srinagar → the houseboat
itinerary.body: Met at the airport and driven straight to Dal Lake. Your houseboat is booked whole — carved cedar, a private deck, and tea whenever you ask for it. The room is decorated for your arrival. Evening is deliberately empty: sit on the deck and watch the lake go orange.

itinerary.title: Sunrise shikara, then the old city
itinerary.body: Out on the water by six, before the lake wakes up — this is the hour the photographs come from. Back for a long breakfast, then the Mughal gardens, Shalimar and Nishat, in the afternoon. Dinner back on the boat.

itinerary.title: Gulmarg — above the treeline
itinerary.body: A two-hour drive up to Gulmarg and the gondola over the pines. In summer it's meadow and wildflowers; in winter you step out into deep snow. Back down to Srinagar for the night, or stay up top if you'd rather — just tell your planner.

itinerary.title: Down to Pahalgam
itinerary.body: The drive follows the Lidder river past saffron fields and cricket-bat workshops. Pahalgam is the slow half of this trip: your room faces the valley, and the plan for the evening is intentionally nothing at all.

itinerary.title: Betaab valley, and the candlelit dinner
itinerary.body: Morning in the Betaab and Aru valleys — pine, meltwater, and very few people if you go early. The candlelit dinner is tonight, set up wherever the property has the best view.

itinerary.title: Srinagar, and home
itinerary.body: An unhurried morning, a stop for saffron and kahwa on the way, and your drop at Srinagar airport.

packages.name: Kerala — Tea Hills & a Houseboat of Your Own
packages.summaryFromDelhi:
KERALA HONEYMOON — MUNNAR, THEKKADY & ALLEPPEY
5 Nights / 6 Days · Private trip for two

Mist on the tea slopes for the first half, water for the second. Munnar for the cold mornings and the endless green, Thekkady for the spice country, then a houseboat in Alleppey that is yours alone — crew, cook, and a sun deck nobody else is on.

The pace is the point. Nothing before 9 AM unless you ask for it.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
The Alleppey houseboat is a private single-bedroom boat, not a shared cabin on a bigger one. The Munnar stay looks straight down a tea valley. Both were picked in person.
packages.socialProof: The houseboat cook made us a fish curry we still talk about. And there was genuinely nobody else on the boat.
packages.scarcityNote: December and January weekends go early.
inclusions: 5 nights stay — 2 Munnar, 1 Thekkady, 1 private Alleppey houseboat, 1 Kochi

Private air-conditioned cab for the whole route

itinerary.title: Kochi → Munnar
itinerary.body: Picked up at Kochi and driven up through rubber and spice country. The last hour is all tea. Your room faces the valley; the evening is yours.

itinerary.title: Munnar, slowly
itinerary.body: Tea estates, the Attukad falls, and Top Station if the sky is clear. Mornings here are genuinely cold — good excuse to stay in longer.

itinerary.title: Thekkady and the spice trail
itinerary.body: Down to Thekkady, a guided walk through cardamom, pepper and vanilla, and a quiet evening in the plantation belt.

itinerary.title: The houseboat
itinerary.body: Board your own houseboat at Alleppey around noon. The boat cruises the narrow canals, moors before sunset, and the crew cooks dinner on board. This is the night people remember.

itinerary.title: Backwater morning → Kochi
itinerary.body: Breakfast on the deck as the boat comes back in, then to Fort Kochi — the Chinese nets, the old streets, and tonight's candlelit dinner.

itinerary.title: Home from Kochi
itinerary.body: A slow breakfast and your drop at Kochi airport.

packages.name: Andaman — Private Shores
packages.summaryFromDelhi:
ANDAMAN HONEYMOON — HAVELOCK & NEIL
5 Nights / 6 Days · Private trip for two

The clearest water in India, and enough time to actually swim in it. Two nights on Havelock for Radhanagar sunsets, two on Neil for the quiet, and the ferries between booked in the good class so the crossings are calm.

Optional scuba for two on Havelock — first-timers welcome, and the instructor holds your hand the entire way down.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
Beach-facing rooms on both islands, not garden view. Private transfers on each island. And the schedule leaves two full afternoons with nothing in them.
packages.socialProof: Radhanagar at sunset, then bioluminescence the same night. Neither of us had seen water glow before.

itinerary.title: Port Blair, and the light show
itinerary.body: Landing, transfer, and an easy evening — Corbyn's Cove, then the sound-and-light show at the Cellular Jail as it gets dark.

itinerary.title: Ferry to Havelock → Radhanagar
itinerary.body: Morning ferry across. Check into a beach-facing room, then Radhanagar for sunset, which is the one everyone has seen a photo of and it still lands.

itinerary.title: Havelock — water day
itinerary.body: Elephant beach by boat for snorkelling, or your scuba dive if you've added it. Afternoon deliberately free.

itinerary.title: Neil Island
itinerary.body: A short ferry to the slow island. Bharatpur for the clear shallows, Laxmanpur for the sunset and the natural rock bridge at low tide.

itinerary.title: Neil, and the beach dinner
itinerary.body: Nothing scheduled until evening, which is the idea. Candlelit dinner set up on the sand tonight.

itinerary.title: Back to Port Blair, and home
itinerary.body: Morning ferry back and your airport drop.

packages.summaryFromDelhi:

The short one — a long weekend that still feels like a proper trip. A lake-facing room in the old city, a private boat on Pichola at golden hour, dinner on a rooftop with the City Palace lit up across the water, and a day out at Kumbhalgarh's ramparts.

Ideal if you have four days, not ten.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
A haveli room actually facing the water, a private sunset boat rather than the shared one, and a planner who books the rooftop table before you arrive.
packages.socialProof: Three days and it still felt unhurried. The rooftop dinner with the palace lit up is the memory.

itinerary.title: Into the old city
itinerary.body: Met and driven to your haveli in the lanes behind Gangaur Ghat. Evening walk to Ambrai ghat for the view back across the water.

itinerary.title: City Palace, then the private boat
itinerary.body: The City Palace and Crystal Gallery in the morning, Saheliyon-ki-Bari after lunch, then your own boat on Pichola for sunset. Rooftop dinner booked for tonight.

itinerary.title: Kumbhalgarh
itinerary.body: Out early to the second-longest continuous wall in the world, and the Ranakpur marble temples on the way back. Back in Udaipur by evening.

packages.name: Spiti Solo Circuit
packages.summaryFromDelhi:
SPITI SOLO CIRCUIT — THE FULL LOOP
7 Nights / 8 Days · Solo-friendly group batch

The big one, and the trip most of our solo travellers pick as their first. A cold desert at 4,000m, monasteries older than most countries, the highest post office in the world, and a night beside Chandratal where the Milky Way is genuinely bright enough to read by.

Batch size is capped at 16. You'll be matched into a twin-share room with someone your own age and gender — no single supplement, ever.

WHO THIS IS FOR
People who booked one seat and want the group to feel like a friend group by day three. It is high altitude, so there's a deliberate acclimatisation night built in.
packages.socialProof: Booked alone, spent eight days with fifteen people I'd now call if I moved cities. Chandratal night is unreal.
packages.scarcityNote: Only 16 seats a batch — June and September fill first.
inclusions: 7 nights stay — hotels, guesthouses and one Chandratal camp
Travel from Delhi and back in a Tempo Traveller
Certified trip captain for the whole batch
Twin-share room matched by age and gender — no single supplement
Bonfire nights where the weather allows
exclusions: Anything personal, and entry tickets at monasteries

itinerary.title: Delhi → Shimla (overnight drive)
itinerary.body: Board in Delhi in the evening. Introductions happen in the first hour and the batch group chat has usually already been going for a week.

itinerary.title: Shimla → Chitkul
itinerary.body: Up the Sutlej valley to the last inhabited village before the Tibet border. Cold, green, and very quiet. First night at altitude.

itinerary.title: Chitkul → Kalpa → Nako
itinerary.body: Kinnaur Kailash from Kalpa at sunrise if the clouds allow, then the landscape turns from pine to bare rock in the space of two hours. Night at Nako.

itinerary.title: Nako → Tabo → Kaza
itinerary.body: Tabo monastery — 1,000 years of continuous use — then Dhankar hanging above the confluence. Into Kaza by evening; this is your acclimatisation base.

itinerary.title: Key, Kibber, Hikkim, Langza
itinerary.body: The postcard day. Key monastery stacked up its hillside, the fossil village at Langza, and a postcard posted from Hikkim at 4,400m — it genuinely arrives.

itinerary.title: Kaza → Chandratal
itinerary.body: Over Kunzum La to the moon lake. No network, no buildings, a camp beside the water. Sleep late — the sky is the reason you came.

itinerary.title: Chandratal → Manali
itinerary.body: Down the Rohtang side through Batal and Gramphu — the roughest and most spectacular stretch of the whole loop. Warm shower and a real bed in Manali.

itinerary.title: Manali → Delhi
itinerary.body: Overnight drive back, arriving Delhi early morning. The group chat does not stop.

packages.name: Kasol & Kheerganga — Solo Batch
packages.summaryFromDelhi:
KASOL & KHEERGANGA — SOLO BATCH
3 Nights / 4 Days · Solo-friendly group batch

The cheapest way to find out whether you like travelling with strangers. A long weekend in the Parvati valley: riverside cafés in Kasol, the walk up to Tosh, and the 12 km climb to the Kheerganga hot spring with a night in a camp at the top.

Leaves Friday night, back Monday morning. You don't have to take leave.

WHO THIS IS FOR
First-time solo travellers. It's short, it's cheap, and the trek is genuinely doable by anyone who walks a bit.
packages.socialProof: Went for a long weekend not knowing a soul. Ended up in the group chat that planned the next four trips.
packages.scarcityNote: Weekend batches fill about ten days out.

itinerary.title: Delhi → Kasol (overnight)
itinerary.body: Friday-night Volvo out of Delhi. You'll have met half the batch before Chandigarh.

itinerary.title: Kasol, Manikaran, Tosh
itinerary.body: Arrive, breakfast by the river, then the hot springs and gurudwara at Manikaran. Afternoon walk up to Tosh for the valley view. Bonfire back in Kasol.

itinerary.title: Kheerganga trek
itinerary.body: 12 km up through pine and waterfalls — four to five hours at an easy pace. The hot spring at the top is at 3,000m, and the camp is right beside it.

itinerary.title: Down, and back to Delhi
itinerary.body: Descend to Barshaini, lunch in Kasol, and the overnight bus home.

packages.destination: Sankri · Juda Ka Talab · Kedarkantha summit
packages.summaryFromDelhi:
KEDARKANTHA — SOLO WINTER TREK
4 Nights / 5 Days · Solo-friendly group batch

India's most-loved beginner winter summit, at 12,500 ft. Deep snow from December, a frozen lake at Juda Ka Talab, and a pre-dawn summit push that puts you on top for sunrise over the Swargarohini range.

No prior trekking experience needed. If you can walk 5 km without stopping, you can do this.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Solo travellers who want the summit photo and the group that comes with it. Batches are capped at 15, with a certified mountain guide plus the trip captain.
packages.socialProof: Summit at sunrise with fourteen people I'd known four days. Half of us cried. Booked Spiti before we got down.

itinerary.title: Dehradun → Sankri
itinerary.body: A long, beautiful drive up the Tons valley. Gear check and briefing at the Sankri guesthouse in the evening.

itinerary.title: Sankri → Juda Ka Talab
itinerary.body: Four hours through oak and pine to a frozen lake at 9,100 ft. First night in a tent, and the first proper snow for most of the batch.

itinerary.title: Juda Ka Talab → Kedarkantha base
itinerary.body: A shorter day up to 11,250 ft, so the afternoon is free for the snow fight that always happens. Early dinner — tomorrow starts in the dark.

itinerary.title: Summit day → Hargaon
itinerary.body: Head torches on at 3 AM. Three hours up in the cold and dark, and then the sun comes over Swargarohini while you're standing on the top. Down to Hargaon camp for the last night.

itinerary.title: Down to Sankri → Dehradun
itinerary.body: A knee-testing descent through the forest, lunch at Sankri, and the drive back to Dehradun by evening.

packages.name: Rishikesh — Solo Weekend

2 Nights / 3 Days · Solo-friendly group batch

The cheapest trip we run, and the one people book when they want to test the water. 16 km of Grade III rapids, a cliff jump if you want it, riverside camping with a bonfire, and the Ganga aarti at Triveni Ghat on the last evening.

Out Friday night, back Monday morning. Under ₹6,000 from Delhi.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Anyone who's never travelled with strangers and wants a low-stakes way to find out. Two nights, one bonfire, and usually a group chat that outlives the trip.
packages.socialProof: Six thousand rupees, one weekend, rapids and a cliff jump. Cheaper than my Friday nights out, honestly.

Living root bridges that take fifteen years to grow, water at Dawki so clear the boats look like they're floating on air, and the cleanest village in Asia. The double-decker root bridge day is 3,500 steps down and 3,500 back up, and it is worth every one of them.

Batch capped at 14, with a local guide who grew up in these villages.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Solo travellers who want somewhere that doesn't look like anywhere else in India. Moderate fitness helps on the root-bridge day.
packages.socialProof: The double-decker bridge day nearly finished me and it's still the best day I've had on a trip.

creators.name: Naman Soni
creators.tagline: Eleven Spiti loops. Same dhaba every time.
creators.bio:
I started posting road-trip videos because I kept getting the same DM: "bhai, is it safe to drive to Spiti in a hatchback?" (It is. Mostly.)

Four years later I've done the Kaza loop eleven times and I still stop at the same dhaba in Nako for rajma chawal, still get altitude-dumb on day three, still cry a little at Chandratal.

What I'm not: a guy who'll make you wake at 5 AM for content. We shoot when the light's good and sleep when it isn't.
creators.quote: I don't want fifteen people watching me make a video. I want fifteen people in the video.
perks: I'm on the bus the whole way — not flying in for a photo op on day four
Free reel edit of your trip: send me your clips, you get a cut back within two weeks
One night I take over the aux and nobody can stop me. This is a perk, not a warning
Camera help whenever you want it — settings, angles, or just someone to hold the phone properly

qa.q: Do I need to be good at photos?
qa.a: No. Roughly half the people who come can't work their own camera app, and by day three they can. That's the whole point of me being there.

qa.q: Is it weird if I'm not on Instagram?
qa.a: Genuinely no. Maybe a third of any batch doesn't post at all. Nobody's counting.

qa.q: Will I actually get to talk to you?
qa.a: You'll get sick of me. It's a Tempo Traveller for eight days — there's nowhere to hide.

qa.q: What if I've never done altitude?
qa.a: Neither had I. There's an acclimatisation night built into the Spiti route, and the captain watches everyone on day three. Drink more water than feels reasonable.

itinerary.title: Delhi → Shimla (overnight drive)
itinerary.body: Board in Delhi with me. I do a proper gear check before we roll — half of you have packed wrong, and that's fine, we fix it at the first stop.

itinerary.title: Shimla → Chitkul
itinerary.body: Up the Sutlej valley to the last inhabited village before the Tibet border. Cold, green, and very quiet. First night at altitude.

itinerary.title: Chitkul → Kalpa → Nako
itinerary.body: Kinnaur Kailash from Kalpa at sunrise if the clouds allow, then the landscape turns from pine to bare rock in the space of two hours. Night at Nako.

itinerary.title: Nako → Tabo → Kaza
itinerary.body: Tabo monastery — 1,000 years of continuous use — then Dhankar hanging above the confluence. Into Kaza by evening; this is your acclimatisation base.

itinerary.title: Key, Kibber, Hikkim, Langza
itinerary.body: The postcard day. Key monastery stacked up its hillside, the fossil village at Langza, and a postcard posted from Hikkim at 4,400m — it genuinely arrives.

itinerary.title: Kaza → Chandratal
itinerary.body: Chandratal night. I shoot the sky here every single trip and I still set up two hours early. Bring the warm layer you think you won't need.

itinerary.title: Chandratal → Manali
itinerary.body: Down the Rohtang side through Batal and Gramphu — the roughest and most spectacular stretch of the whole loop. Warm shower and a real bed in Manali.

itinerary.title: Manali → Delhi
itinerary.body: Overnight drive back, arriving Delhi early morning. The group chat does not stop.

creators.name: Meher Kaul
creators.tagline: I map the routes I wish someone had mapped for me.
creators.bio:
My first solo trip was Kasol in 2021 and I spent most of it on the phone to my mother proving I was alive.

Now I do this full time: I go somewhere, I work out exactly where a woman travelling alone can sleep, eat, walk after dark and get a bus out — and then I write it down properly, because when I needed that page it did not exist.

I'm loud, I ask staff a lot of questions, and I will absolutely make everyone stop for momos.
creators.quote: Half my DMs are one question: will I be okay on my own? Come with me once and you'll stop asking.
perks: Women-only room matching sorted before you board — not negotiated at the hotel desk at midnight
I share the full route with your emergency contact if you want it, before we leave
A proper what-to-pack call the week before, on video, where you can hold things up and ask
I've slept in every stay on these routes. If I wouldn't put my sister there, it's not on the itinerary

qa.q: I've never travelled alone. Is this a bad first attempt?
qa.a: It's the best one. You get the independence of going alone with fourteen people who also came alone, and a captain whose whole job is the boring logistics.
The batches are mixed, the rooms are not. You'll share with women, matched by age. If you'd rather a women-only batch, message me — we run a few every season.
Then you'll have a quiet week with good views, and that's allowed. Nobody makes you do the group games.

qa.q: Periods, safety, all of it — can I ask you?
qa.a: Yes, and please do. That's most of what I get asked and none of it is awkward to me.
